newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries close flat on quiet Christmas Eve.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries close flat on quiet Christmas Eve.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries closed mostly unchanged in extremely thin, uneventful trade as investors squared positions and then stayed mostly sidelined ahead of the Christmas holiday on Wednesday.
The 6-1/2-percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond ended unchanged at 98-28/32 to yield 6.58 percent. The two-year note closed the session flat at 99-26/32, yielding 5.85 percent.
"Trading was really quiet and minimal ... there is no real story out of the price action today," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at consulting firm I.D.E.A Inc.

Analysts said most major players -- money managers, hedge and pension funds -- squared their portfolios in the past few weeks and were now expected to remain out of the market until the end of the year.
"Now it's basically over ... People are going home for the holidays," said a trader at a U.S. investment bank. "Volume is really, really thin and the market is mostly dead."

The market had an abbreviated session on Tuesday ahead of the Christmas holiday. Trading began to wind down by late morning and the market was considered closed at 1400 EST/1900 GMT. The market will remain closed on Wednesday.
Trading will resume on Thursday at normal hours.
The day was also sluggish on the economic data front, with the release of a 1.3 percent rise in the BTM/Schroders' chain store sales index in the week ended December 21.
The Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index will also be announced on Tuesday at its regular release time at 1455 EST/1955 GMT.
The BTM/Schroders data, however, did not have a large impact on the market as players said the picture of sales for the holiday season is still somewhat blurry.
"With the late Thanksgiving ... it's hard to know what kind of a read these data are giving on holiday spending activity," said Richard Berner, chief economist at Mellon Bank Corp.
"My guess is that the numbers are going to come in on the strong side. But whether they correlate to what we see in other data on retail activity is just hard to say," he added.
Analysts said the market is expected to keep its sluggish, holiday tone for the next few sessions.
Spread traders are seen centered on two-year notes and 30-year bonds, whose yield gap is seen trading in a range between 75 and 85 basis points.
Analysts said some unrest might be seen as the market moves into the new year if the economy continues to grow at a moderate to stronger pace.
"If people get a little bit more anxious about Fed policy ... that would probably lend more of a flattening bias to the market," I.D.E.A.'s Stiles said.
The three-month Treasury bill rate closed flat at 4.95 percent. The six-month bill rate fell two basis points to 5.06 percent. The year bill rate was down two points at 5.20 percent.
The five-year note traded unchanged at 99-31/32 to yield 6.13 percent. The ten-year note closed unchanged at 101-4/32, yielding 6.34 percent.
